title: Support cross-realm WebAssembly.Module CSP checks through serialization
body: This updates `creating a WebAssembly module script` to support a creation path from an existing `WebAssembly.Module` to be used when deserializing a `WebAssembly.Module` in another realm. The reason for this is to ensure correct CSP policy integration through modules that are transferred from one realm to another, while possibly having differing CSP policy values for `script-src` and `wasm-unsafe-eval`. For example, if a `WebAssembly.Module` was imported in a realm whose `script-src` policy allows its URL, but then it is transferred to a realm with a different `script-src` policy - we must check the module against this script source policy on instantiation. At the same time, the WebAssembly CSP specification is moving to gating instantiation of modules per https://github.com/WebAssembly/content-security-policy/issues/48 and as discussed recently in the CG. For the ESM Integration's script-src policy not to break under this, we need to now distinguish modules which were compiled on the realm they exist in, and that therefore do not need to have their CSP policy "re-checked" on instantiation. This "re-checking" can only support re-checking `script-src` and `wasm-unsafe-eval` policies against the target realm a transferred module is instantiated within. Modules loaded through a nonce or `'strict-dynamic'` would also fail any re-check. To distinguish modules loaded on the current realm, which were already CSP-checked, versus deserialized modules, we do this by: 1. `fetch a single module script` will set a new `realm loaded` boolean marking the module as CSP checked only on the current realm 2. `creating a WebAssembly module script` supports a new variant receiving a `WebAssembly.Module` object directly, and populating its `[[HostDefined]]` on its ECMA-262 module record with a script record, but with `realm loaded` set to *false*, which is then used by the deserialization spec for `WebAssembly.Module` specified in the ESM integration. As a result, a corresponding CSP update is then able to skip CSP-checking for WebAssembly.instantiate for ESM Integration modules in the same realm they were originally compiled, while supporting a new check for them in transfer against their final `baseURL` value. * WebAssembly/esm-integration#131 is the corresponding ESM Integration change written against this new `create a WebAssembly Module Record` call. * https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-csp/issues/834 is the corresponding CSP spec change to support re-checking the CSP policy during instantiation from the original module script optionally in the Wasm CSP hook There is no check here for a module source passed to `import()` or `new Worker()`. That belongs in the Module Record branch of HostLoadImportedModule, which only exists in #11152, so it will be added there using the same CSP check, where it covers JavaScript module sources too. - [ ] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * … * … - [ ] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * … - [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: … * Gecko: … * WebKit: … * Deno (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, module resolution, web workers, and web storage): … * Node.js (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, and module resolution): … - [ ] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: - [ ] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: … - [ ] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
